definition: A feature that allows users or organizations to create and manage multiple separate workspaces or environments within a single platform.
extendedDefinition: A feature that allows users or organizations to create and manage multiple separate workspaces or environments within a single platform. Multi-workspace support lets one account run several isolated spaces, useful for agencies serving multiple clients, franchises managing locations, and organizations separating teams, projects, or environments. Isolation is the core value: each workspace can hold its own members, permissions, data, and branding, preventing cross-contamination while keeping administrative overhead low. Buyers should examine how membership and billing span workspaces, whether data can move between them with governance, and how the vendor walls off access. Workspace sprawl is a real risk: without governance, orphaned spaces accumulate licenses and unmanaged data. Evaluation questions include transfer of ownership, archiving, and export per workspace, plus the cost of cross-workspace sharing when collaboration across teams is required. Clear workspace governance, including naming, ownership, and lifecycle policy, keeps the flexibility from becoming administrative debt.
